scenes.tts: If every division keeps some daughters and spends others, how many neurons does the cortex get?
scenes.visual: Title card fades. A tally counter sits beside a single radial glial cell.
scenes.narration: If every division keeps some daughters and spends others, how many neurons does the cortex get?

scenes.tts: Start with a simple model. A pool of dividing cells, each dividing once per round, with none dying. Every cell makes two daughters.
scenes.visual: N cells divide into 2N daughters, shown as dots. Corner tag: simple model; one round = one cell cycle for the pool; no cell death.
scenes.narration: Start with a simple model. A pool of dividing cells, each dividing once per round, with none dying. Every cell makes two daughters.

scenes.tts: Call P the fraction of daughters that stay progenitors. Call Q the fraction that quit as neurons. Together they make one.
scenes.visual: The daughters sort into two groups, labelled P (stay) and Q (quit). Equation on screen: P + Q = 1.
scenes.narration: Call P the fraction of daughters that stay progenitors. Call Q the fraction that quit as neurons. Together they make one.

scenes.tts: The next pool comes from the daughters that stay. The neurons come from the daughters that quit. This pool is every dividing cell, not just stem cells.
scenes.visual: On screen: next pool = 2N × P; neurons made this round = 2N × Q. Note under the pool: all dividing cells (radial glia + intermediate progenitors).
scenes.narration: The next pool comes from the daughters that stay. The neurons come from the daughters that quit. This pool is every dividing cell, not just stem cells.

scenes.tts: Suppose Q is one half. Half the daughters quit. Does the pool shrink, hold or grow? And does it make neurons?
scenes.caption: Suppose Q is 0.5. Half the daughters quit. Does the pool shrink, hold or grow? And does it make neurons?
scenes.visual: A slider set to Q = 0.5. Pool counter and neuron counter both show question marks.
scenes.narration: Suppose Q is 0.5. Half the daughters quit. Does the pool shrink, hold or grow? And does it make neurons?

scenes.tts: It holds, and it makes neurons. It is as if every division keeps one daughter and spends one. A steady pool is not an idle one.
scenes.visual: Pool counter stays at N; neuron counter rises by N each cycle.
scenes.narration: It holds, and it makes neurons. It is as if every division keeps one daughter and spends one. A steady pool is not an idle one.

scenes.tts: Below one half, the pool grows. Above it, the pool shrinks.
scenes.caption: Below 0.5, the pool grows. Above it, the pool shrinks.
scenes.visual: The slider moves left: the pool grows. Right: the pool shrinks.
scenes.narration: Below 0.5, the pool grows. Above it, the pool shrinks.

scenes.tts: In mouse dorsal cortex, Takahashi and colleagues estimated about eleven cycles of neurogenesis.
scenes.visual: A row of eleven cycle boxes. Tag: Takahashi, Nowakowski and Caviness.
scenes.narration: In mouse dorsal cortex, Takahashi and colleagues estimated about eleven cycles of neurogenesis.

scenes.tts: Q starts near zero. It passes one half in the eighth cycle, and reaches about point eight by the tenth.
scenes.caption: Q starts near zero. It passes 0.5 in the eighth cycle, and reaches about 0.8 by the tenth.
scenes.visual: The Q slider climbs across the boxes: near 0 at cycle 1, past 0.5 at cycle 8, about 0.8 at cycle 10.
scenes.narration: Q starts near zero. It passes 0.5 in the eighth cycle, and reaches about 0.8 by the tenth.

scenes.tts: Takahashi measured Q for the ventricular zone proper, apart from cells dividing farther out. Those old compartments are not today's cell classes.
scenes.visual: The Q slider gets a tag: ventricular zone estimate; not a direct count of stem cells kept.
scenes.narration: Takahashi measured Q for the ventricular zone proper, apart from cells dividing farther out. Those old compartments are not today's cell classes.

scenes.tts: Follow one founder through that schedule. The numbers are illustrative.
scenes.visual: Two curves start to draw, labelled pool and neurons made. Corner tag: illustrative model.
scenes.narration: Follow one founder through that schedule. The numbers are illustrative.

scenes.tts: Early on, almost nothing is made, and the pool multiplies.
scenes.visual: The pool curve rises through the early rounds. The neuron curve, labelled neurons made this round, stays small through round 4, then climbs to about 23 in round 7.
scenes.narration: Early on, almost nothing is made, and the pool multiplies.

scenes.tts: Late, the pool is spent. Output peaks at cycle nine, just after Q passes one half, while the pool is still near its largest.
scenes.caption: Late, the pool is spent. Output peaks at cycle 9, just after Q passes 0.5, while the pool is still near its largest.
scenes.visual: The pool curve tops out and falls; the neuron curve peaks at cycle 9 (marked). About 150 neurons in all.
scenes.narration: Late, the pool is spent. Output peaks at cycle 9, just after Q passes 0.5, while the pool is still near its largest.

scenes.tts: The schedule is a lever. In this model, moving the crossing one cycle later nearly doubles the total, over the same eleven cycles.
scenes.visual: The Q = 0.5 crossing slides one cycle right; the total-neurons bar grows to about 1.8 times. Small tag: same eleven cycles; about a dozen cells still dividing.
scenes.narration: The schedule is a lever. In this model, moving the crossing one cycle later nearly doubles the total, over the same eleven cycles.

scenes.tts: That is why a few extra proliferative cycles are a candidate for how bigger cortices are built.
scenes.visual: A small mouse cortex beside a larger one. Label: a candidate, see human brain expansion.
scenes.narration: That is why a few extra proliferative cycles are a candidate for how bigger cortices are built.

scenes.tts: Now a trap. Suppose every radial glial division makes a radial glial cell and an intermediate progenitor.
scenes.visual: One radial glial cell divides into a radial glial cell and an intermediate progenitor.
scenes.narration: Now a trap. Suppose every radial glial division makes a radial glial cell and an intermediate progenitor.

scenes.tts: In that round, no daughter quits. Counted as one pool, it seems to double.
scenes.visual: A single lumped counter jumps from 1 to 2. Q = 0 on screen.
scenes.narration: In that round, no daughter quits. Counted as one pool, it seems to double.

scenes.tts: Follow one radial glial cell for four cycles. Each intermediate progenitor divides into two neurons. How many radial glia, and how many neurons?
scenes.visual: Four empty cycle boxes; two separate counters labelled radial glia and neurons, both with question marks.
scenes.narration: Follow one radial glial cell for four cycles. Each intermediate progenitor divides into two neurons. How many radial glia, and how many neurons?

scenes.tts: Still one radial glial cell, and six neurons. One more intermediate progenitor is about to make two more. That first doubling was not a gain in stem cells.
scenes.visual: The boxes fill: radial glia stays at 1; neurons go 0, 2, 4, 6; one intermediate progenitor waits to divide.
scenes.narration: Still one radial glial cell, and six neurons. One more intermediate progenitor is about to make two more. That first doubling was not a gain in stem cells.

scenes.tts: So count two pools. In this model, radial glia are the source that keeps neurogenesis going.
scenes.visual: The two counters separate. Label on the radial glia counter: keeps the source going.
scenes.narration: So count two pools. In this model, radial glia are the source that keeps neurogenesis going.

scenes.tts: Intermediate progenitors multiply, and delay, what each spent daughter yields.
scenes.visual: Label on the intermediate progenitor branch: multiplies and delays output.
scenes.narration: Intermediate progenitors multiply, and delay, what each spent daughter yields.

scenes.tts: The cycle itself slows. In mouse dorsal cortex, it lengthens from about eight hours to about eighteen. Nearly all the added time is in G one.
scenes.caption: The cycle itself slows. In mouse dorsal cortex, it lengthens from about 8 hours to about 18. Nearly all the added time is in G1.
scenes.visual: A cell-cycle bar stretches from about 8 h to about 18 h; the G1 segment grows the most.
scenes.narration: The cycle itself slows. In mouse dorsal cortex, it lengthens from about 8 hours to about 18. Nearly all the added time is in G1.

scenes.tts: One hypothesis: a longer G one gives fate determinants more time to act.
scenes.caption: One hypothesis: a longer G1 gives fate determinants more time to act.
scenes.visual: Label beside the long G1 segment: hypothesis, more time for fate determinants.
scenes.narration: One hypothesis: a longer G1 gives fate determinants more time to act.

scenes.tts: In cultured mouse embryos, a drug that lengthened G one led to early neurogenesis. Whether a longer G one causes the switch is still open.
scenes.caption: In cultured mouse embryos, a drug that lengthened G1 led to early neurogenesis. Whether a longer G1 causes the switch is still open.
scenes.visual: A culture dish with a mouse embryo; early neurons appear. Tag: Calegari and Huttner, 2003. Label: cause or consequence? open.
scenes.narration: In cultured mouse embryos, a drug that lengthened G1 led to early neurogenesis. Whether a longer G1 causes the switch is still open.

scenes.tts: The first puzzle has an answer: the scaffold is the source. The second has a partial answer: the trip to the ventricle fits the centrosome and may let more cells share the surface.
scenes.visual: The two puzzle cards from chapter one return: puzzle 1 gets a check mark, puzzle 2 a half check (partly settled).
scenes.narration: The first puzzle has an answer: the scaffold is the source. The second has a partial answer: the trip to the ventricle fits the centrosome and may let more cells share the surface.

scenes.tts: What the cortex gets is a count: how many radial glia each division keeps, and what each spent daughter yields.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: keep two, one or none; one neuron, or usually two, per spent daughter.
scenes.narration: What the cortex gets is a count: how many radial glia each division keeps, and what each spent daughter yields.
